Nothing is wrong or misleading.

Finding 4 (the wheels' Reset is hidden while an action is selected): already covered in 'Grading inside an action', which says a grade section's header shows Clear in place of Reset while an action is selected. That holds for every section, so repeating it under Wheels adds nothing. The not-differing half of the same code is handled by finding 14's edit to the general header sentence.

app_defects.title: The Camera Log double-conversion warning shows on any PQ file with a LUT look, even with no Camera Log set
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/VideoPane+Look.swift:29-37 tests only snapshot.media(media)?.color != nil. Import stores MediaColor(pq: ...) on every PQ file (app/Sources/MediaImporter+Color.swift:39-60, MediaImporter.swift detectedPQ), so color is non-nil without log or lut. The warning 'This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice.' is then false. The test should read color.log != nil || color.lut != nil. The guide now describes the current behaviour.

app_defects.title: Removing a LUT named by an action's end strips the clip's own look at the action's end, though the code calls such an end inert
app_defects.evidence: core/src/actions.rs:486-491 replaces a merged look that fails evaluates_as_look (core/src/lut.rs:192) with null, rather than falling back to the base look. A clip with base look Warm and an end naming the removed LUT therefore loses Warm from the action's end onward. The comments in actions.rs:475-483 and in lut.rs's module doc ('ends are left alone (inert by the evaluator)') say inert. Reachable through set_action_end, or through an end written before the clip's look was changed. The guide now describes the current behaviour.

app_defects.title: A qualifier range can't be turned off inside an action: the checkbox, the row's default item and a near-grey pick all do nothing to a range the clip has on
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/VideoPane+Qualifier.swift:79 (checkbox) and :99 (row default, shown as 'Set end value to default' on a row that animates, app/Sources/InspectorRowMenu.swift:79) and app/Sources/QualifierProps.swift:337 (near-grey pick) all send a null through binding.ops(video:) to set_action_end. core/src/edit_action.rs:339-340 prune_removed (core/src/edit_action_end.rs:20-36) deletes that key from the end, so nothing turns off at the action's end. With a range on on the clip and none in the end, the menu item stays enabled (differs: on) and has no effect. The guide now states the limit.

app_defects.title: ColorWheelControl's comment understates the wheel's offset from the vectorscope in an HLG project
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/ColorWheelControl.swift:13 says 'every 75 % target within 12°', with hueRotation fixed at 103 (:31). Computed offsets: yellow and blue are 11.8° off on Rec. 709 and 12.4° off with BT.2020 weights, so the claim is false in an HLG project. Comment only, no user-visible effect beyond the approximate alignment.

A clip with base look Warm and an end naming the removed LUT therefore loses Warm from the action's end onward. The comments in actions.rs:475-483 and in lut.rs's module doc ('ends are left alone (inert by the evaluator)') say inert. Reachable through set_action_end, or through an end written before the clip's look was changed. The guide now describes the current behaviour.

app_defects.title: A qualifier range can't be turned off inside an action: the checkbox, the row's default item and a near-grey pick all do nothing to a range the clip has on
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/VideoPane+Qualifier.swift:79 (checkbox) and :99 (row default, shown as 'Set end value to default' on a row that animates, app/Sources/InspectorRowMenu.swift:79) and app/Sources/QualifierProps.swift:337 (near-grey pick) all send a null through binding.ops(video:) to set_action_end. core/src/edit_action.rs:339-340 prune_removed (core/src/edit_action_end.rs:20-36) deletes that key from the end, so nothing turns off at the action's end. With a range on on the clip and none in the end, the menu item stays enabled (differs: on) and has no effect. The guide now states the limit.

app_defects.title: ColorWheelControl's comment understates the wheel's offset from the vectorscope in an HLG project
app_defects.evidence: app/Sources/ColorWheelControl.swift:13 says 'every 75 % target within 12°', with hueRotation fixed at 103 (:31). Computed offsets: yellow and blue are 11.8° off on Rec. 709 and 12.4° off with BT.2020 weights, so the claim is false in an HLG project. Comment only, no user-visible effect beyond the approximate alignment.
